candidates: When adding documentation for a new feature variant in Mermaid syntax docs (e.g., `packages/mermaid/src/docs/syntax/gitgraph.md`), preserve all pre-existing examples alongside new ones rather than replacing them — every supported use case should have at least one worked example in the documentation.

Never remove or modify existing grammar rules in `packages/mermaid/src/diagrams/git/parser/gitGraph.jison`; only append new rules. A core Mermaid principle is that previously valid diagram syntax must continue to parse correctly — dropping a rule is a breaking change.

Use ES6 template literals (`` `text ${variable}` ``) instead of string concatenation when constructing multi-part strings in JavaScript source files; avoid `'text ' + variable + ' more text'` patterns.

Only attach an `error.hash` object when throwing an error if every hash field (`text`, `token`, `line`, `loc`, `expected`) can be accurately populated from the available context; if correct values are not available, omit the hash entirely rather than filling it with placeholder or incorrect data.

In `cherryPick` (`gitGraphAst.js`), the validation that `parentCommitId` refers to an actual immediate parent of the source commit must run whenever `parentCommitId` is supplied, regardless of whether the source commit is of type `commitType.MERGE` — do not gate this check inside the MERGE-type branch, or a diagram that passes an invalid `parent:` on a non-merge cherry-pick will silently succeed.

When adding optional or order-independent arguments to statement rules in `packages/mermaid/src/diagrams/git/parser/gitGraph.jison`, define reusable sub-rules for each argument alternative rather than enumerating every permutation of argument order as separate top-level productions; this prevents combinatorial explosion as more options are added.
